newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on soybean rally, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on soybean rally, exports.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended higher on Thursday, pulled up by soybeans with USDA weekly export sales data also lending support, traders said.
Floor traders also pointed to ideas Wednesday's massive selloff was overdone and to a lack of fund selling.
The U.S. Agriculture Department on Thursday put weekly old crop corn sales at 589,800 tonnes, above trade expectations for 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
New crop corn sales of 417,700 tonnes were at the low end of the range of expectations.
Strength in soybeans was cited as a supportive factor.
Soybeans ended higher amid rumors China was looking to buy U.S. soybeans but U.S. exporters could not confirm the rumors.

New crop drew strength from the National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook released Wednesday, which called for normal to below normal temperatures across the U.S. Midwest and normal to above normal precipitation. Persistent cool, wet weather could slow crop development, traders said.
Corn ended three to 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher with July up three at $2.74-1/4.
World grain production figures released Thursday by the International Grains Council capped gains, traders said.

IGC forecast a six million tonne increase in world coarse grain production to a record 903 million tonnes. The increase was mainly due to higher crop expectations in the United States, particularly corn.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought three million bushels December. Merrill Lynch bought three million July and SAK Futures bought four million July.

In options trade, Lind-Waldock sold 1,000 December $2.50 puts at 11-1/2 to 11 cents, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold 500 July $2.80 puts at 10 cents and CIS sold 500 December $3.20 calls at 3-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 53,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 60,595.
